messages:
emma_support: FYI - escalating ticket TKT-12345 from ACME. They report intermittent 401s during GitHub SSO after redirect. Happens ~10-30s after clicking sign-in. Repro steps attached.

liam_eng: Can you paste the exact callback URL they registered and the callback we see hit our app? Also want the raw request/response for the token exchange (no redaction of params besides client_secret).

emma_support: Registered app callback: https://acme.example.com/auth/callback
We see the browser hit /auth/callback with a query `?code=XXXX&state=st_abc` then a client-side redirect to /auth/complete. Ticket says sometimes code never reaches our server and then exchange fails with 400 invalid_grant. Here's the token exchange log (scrubbed):
```
POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
body: grant_type=authorization_code&code=&code_verifier=&redirect_uri=https://acme.example.com/auth/callback
response: 400 {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"code not found"}
```

olivia_se: Customer uses a link shortener (https://lnk.acme) in marketing and also uses it in their mobile app to deep link into the site. Could be fragment vs query handling or the shortener adding a fragment.

liam_eng: That matches a classic PKCE/code loss flow - if the auth code ends up in the URL fragment (#code=...) the browser will not send it to the server on redirect. Some link shorteners turn query params into fragments when rewriting deep links.

emma_support: Interesting — their repro steps: open app -> click GH login -> webview to github -> authorise -> redirect back to lnk.acme/redirect?code=... which then 302s to acme.example.com#code=... (we sometimes see code= in query, sometimes in fragment).

liam_eng: A few investigative leads:
- Check if any intermediate CDN or proxy rewrites `?code=` to `#code=` or strips `code_verifier` on POST.
- Confirm whether the client uses the PKCE flow (it should send code_verifier from localStorage) and whether that value is present when the server performs exchange.
- If the mobile/webview uses a JS handler to move fragment -> server, race windows can drop the code if navigation happens too quickly.

emma_support: I pulled nginx proxy access logs from their frontend (attached). There's a 302 from /redirect to acme.example.com/auth/callback with Location: https://acme.example.com/auth/callback#_=_&code=...
Also saw a few entries where our API endpoint /oauth/token received body with empty code_verifier.

liam_eng: That 302 is the smoking gun. Fragment identifiers never sent to origin servers. If the link shortener or their redirector is rewriting the callback to use a fragment, the server won't get the code. If the JS on the callback page is supposed to read the fragment and POST to the server, make sure that happens before any navigation or auto-submit.

olivia_se: Quick mitigation for customer: update their GitHub OAuth app to use a callback that includes a short stable path (they already do), but more importantly disable the link shortener for auth flows or ensure the shortener preserves query params. Also add a fallback where the client reads window.location.hash and sends it to /auth/complete via POST with the code_verifier included.

liam_eng: Also check for any caching layer that might cache the initial redirect response (weird but I've seen CDNs cache 302 bodies). If a cached redirect rewrites to a fragment, that could intermittently break newer flows.

emma_support: Customer confirmed they disabled lnk.acme redirects for the auth button and tested — sign-in now stable for 24h. They still want a fix so they can keep shortener.

liam_eng: For a long-term fix we should advise them to: 1) ensure shortener preserves querystring and doesn't convert to fragment, 2) make the callback page robust: if code in fragment, client JS must POST code+code_verifier to server before any navigation, and 3) tighten redirect URI exact-match rules in GitHub app so intermediates can't inject fragments.

olivia_se: Filed internal follow-up INC-789 for docs/guide: "Auth with link shorteners and mobile deep links" + checklist for PKCE flows in webview/mobile. I'll draft a KB we can share. :white_check_mark:

emma_support: Marking TKT-12345 resolved (customer confirmed). Adding notes to ticket and asking them to re-enable shortener after testing with our checklist. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

bot-deploy: Reminder: please tag any changes to docs in the auth-playbook repo so oncall can review.
